description.narrative:
Insatsen är en andra fas av National Integrity Building and Anti-corruption Program (NIBA), implementerat av Centre for Transparency and Accountability in Liberia (CENTAL). Programmet bygger på resultat från det tidigare stödet till CENTALs NIBA-program (2020-2023). Totala budgeten för insatsen är 15 MSEK.
Det övergripande syftet med programmet är att "bidra till att bygga och upprätthålla ett Liberia där medborgare agerar med öppenhet och integritet i alla sina handlingar". Detta kommer att uppnås genom att fokusera både på att öka insynen och integriteten hos offentliga institutioner, men också genom att öka medborgarnas engagemang för att upprätthålla integritet och transparens. Dessutom kommer fokus ligga på att fortsätta stärka kapaciteten hos CENTAL.
Tre delmål bidrar till det övergripande målet:
1) Att öka transparensen och integriteten inom offentliga institutioner i Liberia, särskilt de som tillhandahåller offentliga tjänster;
2) Att öka medborgarnas handlingar för att upprätthålla integritet och transparens;
3) Att öka CENTALs inflytande och organisatoriska hållbarhet inom anti-korruptionsområdet.
Målgrupperna som insatsen fokuserar på är integritets-institutioner, Nationella Integritetsforumet (NIF), rättsväsendet, lagstiftare, kvinnogrupper, ungdomsgrupper, personer med funktionsnedsättning och särskilda behov, media och civilsamhället inklusive organisationer på lokal nivå..

The contribution is supporting a second phase of the National Integrity Building and Anti-corruption Program (NIBA), implemented by the Center for Transparency and Accountability in Liberia (CENTAL). The program builds on the results from the previous support to CENTAL's NIBA-program (2020-2023). The total budget of the program amounts to 15 MSEK.
The overall aim of the program is to "Contribute to building and sustaining a Liberia where Citizens Act with Transparency and Integrity in All their Dealings". This will be reached by focusing both on increasing transparency and integrity of public sector institutions, but also by increasing citizens' action in upholding integrity and transparency. Additionally, there will be a focus on continuing strengthening the capacity of CENTAL.
Three objectives are contributing towards the program goal:
1) To increase transparency and integrity of public sector institutions in Liberia, especially those providing public services;
2) To increase citizens’ actions in upholding integrity and transparency;
3) To increase CENTAL's influence and organizational sustainability in the anti-corruption space.
The target groups reached by the contribution are public integrity institutions (LACC, GAC, PPCC, IAA, LEITI and Ministry of Justice), National Integrity Forum (NIF), Judiciary, Legislature, County Leaderships, Women Groups, Youth Groups, Persons with disabilities and special needs, Media and Civil Society and Community based Organizations.

The program focuses on three objectives, which all contribute to the overall program goal of "Contribute to building and sustaining a Liberia where Citizens Act with Transparency and Integrity in All their Dealings".
The three objectives are:
1) To increase transparency and integrity of public sector institutions in Liberia, especially those providing public services by December 2026;
2) To increase citizens actions in upholding integrity and transparency in Liberia by December 2026; and
3) To increase CENTAL's influence and organizational sustainability in the anti-corruption space in Liberia by December 2026

title.narrative: Grant Agreement between Sida and CENTAL regarding National Integrity Building and Anti-Corruption Program (NIBA) Phase II

description.narrative:
Examples of results during the first year of implementation (2024):
- A total of 13,356 individuals were reached through different types of activities in the seven target counties. Of these individuals, 49.7 percent were females. Also, more than 70 percent are young people (35 years and below).
- The advocacy and legal advice center (ALAC) strengthened its engagement with public institutions and local communities and held training sessions with several government institutions including Liberia National Police (LNP), Liberia Electricity Corporation (LEC) and Liberia Water and Sewer Corporation (LWSC). Through these trainings, civil servants were exposed to the dangers, consequences, and penalties for corruption as well as the benefits of embedding anticorruption measures in public service delivery.
- The Corruption Case Tracker (CCT) was launched to monitor corruption cases across the prosecution chain. This tracker serves to spur advocacy for speedy action and to increase transparency and institutional collaboration.
- ALAC received 877 hotline calls. Legal aid was provided in 56 cases with interventions sometimes leading to financial recoveries for affected communities. Three cases were forwarded to Liberia Anti-Corruption Commission (LACC), one to Ministry of Internal Affairs (MIA) and one to Financial Intelligence Agency (FIA).
- A total of 54 episodes of the Integrity Watch radio program were broadcasted and aired on Truth FM and ECOWAS Radio. This generated citizen calls and covered topics such as public financial management and procurement reforms.
- 20 stakeholder engagements involving policy makers, heads of public institutions, civil society organizations, and local leaders were held. These engagements aimed to foster and strengthen partnerships between the government of Liberia and civil society organizations to combat corruption, promote good governance, and embed a culture of integrity at the national level. Additionally, these interactions served as platforms to disseminate findings from the State of Corruption Report and advocate for a more robust transparency sector.
- Meetings were also held with legislators, including with the (then) Speaker of the House of Representatives. A meeting with Senator Amara Konneh led to him opening a website to increase transparency around his activities.
- A policy dialogue focusing on financing anticorruption and advocating for increased funding for Liberia's integrity institutions and strengthened anticorruption mechanisms, was held with great attendance from the legislature, integrity institutions, civil society and international partners. After the dialogue, the budget for integrity institutions increased by 1.7 MUSD (total 22.89 MUSD).
- Joint Civil Society Anti-Corruption Initiative (JOCSAI) implemented several key anticorruption initiatives, including a transparency dialogue in Paynesville that led to improved waste management services and eight community-based discussions across Montserrado, which resulted in calls for audits and leadership accountability.
- Internally, CENTAL has developed four key policies: Information and Technology (IT), standalone AntiCorruption, Conflict of Interest, and Leave policies. These policies enhance operational efficiency, uphold ethical standards, and reinforce anticorruption measures.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
